newsitem.title: USA: Gunman vanishes as police storm Navy base bank.
newsitem.headline: Gunman vanishes as police storm Navy base bank.

text.p: Military police and FBI agents were searching for a masked gunman after a bungled bank robbery attempt at a nuclear submarine base on Wednesday.
The gunman apparently was long gone by the time heavily armed police stormed the bank, which they had surrounded for four hours, fearing the gunman might be hiding inside.
The incident began about 8 a.m. PDT when the gunman accosted an employee who was opening the Kitsap Bank branch on Bangor Submarine Naval Base near Seattle, Navy officials said.
The gunman ordered the woman to lie on the floor while he attempted unsuccessfully to get cash out of the night-drop box and teller drawers.
After about 10 minutes the employee was able to call base security and the building quickly was surrounded by police, who maintained telephone contact with the woman inside.
Finally at noon a Washington State Patrol SWAT team swept through the bank but found no trace of the gunman.

The base, on the Hood Canal near Silverdale, about 20 miles west of Seattle, serves as the West Coast home for the nation's fleet of Trident nuclear submarines and employs about 11,000 military and civilian personnel.
